title: Alembic post-D14 long-horizon interface governance sequence
evidenceBinding: D15-D32 must consume the P01-P15 concrete problem map from the design basis. Each demand must either fix, preserve-with-owner, defer-by-decision, or block each applicable problem; do not add demands or docs for length alone.
purpose: After D8-D14 complete, continue D15-D32 as a long-horizon unattended interface governance and cleanup queue: current-state analysis, responsibility split, interface reasonability, parameter/data content audit, detailed product rewrites, consumer-driven validation, deletion proof, drift gates, runtime scenario validation, and final archive.
philosophy: This is optimization, not feature reduction. D15-D18 decide from real code and evidence; D19-D30 implement and harden by ownership; D31-D32 validate and accept. No demand may create thin interfaces, static mocks, docs-only shells, or delete functionality without no-consumer proof and replacement validation.
preClaimGate: Claim D15 only after D14 completes, or after the controller explicitly blocks D14 and the user asks for post-D14 continuation despite that blocker.
Do not use D15-D32 to bypass D8-D14 implementation or acceptance.
D15-D18 must produce evidence-backed decisions before product rewrite demands D19-D23 are dispatched.
D19-D30 may proceed unattended only while each claimed demand is covered by the confirmed D15+ design, state root, and repository ownership.
D31-D32 require raw evidence review and must not accept target summaries without command/runtime/fixture/UI evidence.
globalUserDecisions: D15+ is a long-term real landing plan, not only a current-state audit.
The goal includes more detailed interface optimization, responsibility split, semantic clarity, parameter/data content correction, and continuous unattended development.
Preserve full functionality; optimization cannot thin, mock, hide, or downgrade real behavior.
No arbitrary character gate or truncation logic is the primary goal; the goal is clean, purposeful, schema-backed interfaces.
Do not keep old-version compatibility by default; keep only current-consumer compatibility with owner and cleanup trigger.
Version/evolution strategy remains deferred unless the user explicitly reopens it.
claimRules: Claim at most one demand at a time.
Do not dispatch from this manifest alone; create a state root for the claimed demand first.
D15 precedes D16, D16 precedes D17, and D17 precedes D18.
D18 must slice product implementation before D19-D23 product windows are dispatched.
D24 uses D19-D23 outputs to create consumer-driven replay evidence.
D25-D30 use D24 evidence plus product-window evidence to harden taxonomy, capabilities, diagnostics, sensitive fields, deletion, and drift gates.
D31 validates real runtime/Dashboard/MCP scenarios after D19-D30.
D32 accepts, blocks, archives, or extracts new out-of-scope backlog only after raw evidence review.
